title: Nth Fibonacci number
instructorPromptText: Write a function that returns the nth Fibonacci number, where fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1.

specGateDimensions.description: What should the function do if n is negative?
specGateDimensions.rationale: The prompt defines the sequence for n=0 and n=1 but says nothing about negative n; the student must commit to raising, returning 0, or treating it as undefined behavior before coding.

specGateDimensions.description: What happens if n is not an integer (a float like 3.0, a string, None)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Type contract is a common blind spot; surfacing it in the spec prevents 'it crashed' being treated as a separate bug later.

specGateDimensions.description: Will the function compute fib(n) recursively, iteratively, or with memoization — and does the spec care, or only about the return value?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Fibonacci is the canonical exercise where naive recursion is exponentially slow; the student should decide whether performance is part of the contract or only correctness.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Spec says fib(0) = 0 but code's recursive base case returns 1 for n <= 1, shifting the whole sequence by one
Student writes naive recursion that is correct but hangs for n=40+; spec did not mention performance so student calls it done, but the function is unusable for realistic inputs
Plan describes recursion; code uses an iterative loop with two accumulator variables — coherent switch to a more efficient strategy
Plan describes iteration; code uses functools.lru_cache on a recursive definition — coherent memoization refactor
Off-by-one in iterative version: loop runs n times instead of n-1 times (or vice versa), so fib(5) returns fib(4) or fib(6)
Recursive call uses fib(n) + fib(n-1) instead of fib(n-1) + fib(n-2), causing infinite recursion or wrong values
Iterative version initializes a, b = 1, 1 instead of 0, 1, producing the sequence starting from fib(1) and breaking the fib(0) = 0 contract
